history.dynasty: Cochin rulers (19th-century renovation); earlier administration by six Moosad families (Parasudayavar)
history.period: Ancient - founding date undocumented; current structure largely a late-19th-century Cochin renovation after a fire
history.summary: Rare dual Rama-Lakshmana temple atop a ~100 ft hillock near the Bharathappuzha river, one of the four major Rama temples of Kerala (with Thriprayar, Kadavallur and Thiruvangad), administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board. Legend holds the east-facing (Lakshmana) idol was an image of Vishnu worshipped by Shiva, handed to his disciple Parasurama, who consecrated it here after creating Kerala; the west-facing (Rama) idol manifested as swayambhu before sage Amalaka (who lived only on gooseberries) at Saraswathi kundu. Both idols are of the rare Pathalanjana Sila stone; Rama's gold-covered kavacham is never removed, and the temple has no kodimaram (flagstaff). The origin legends are recorded in the 18-chapter 'Sri Vilwadri Mahatmya'. Historically the temple was attacked by Tipu Sultan's armies in the 18th century, renovated in the mid-19th century, then gutted by fire and rebuilt by the Cochin rulers in the late 19th century; two seven-storey gopurams were once destroyed by lightning and never rebuilt. name: Thiruvilwamala Rama Temple
town_description: Thiruvilwamala is a hill town in Thrissur district, Kerala, near the Bharathappuzha river. Its name comes from the sacred vilwa (bael) tree, and it is dominated by the hilltop Vilwadrinatha temple, reached by over 50 steps.
